title: Ghost Type
description: Christina Rossetti’s “Who Has Seen the Wind?” set huge as a justified block of heavy type. Pull any word out and it trails outlined ghosts that ripple like cloth; let go and it flies home along a curve while the line opens its gap to take it back.
intent: Type as cloth in the wind: one heavy word at a time leaves the block, its speed drawn as computed outline ghosts and a one-pixel slice bend, and the block re-justifies around it without ever jumping.

sources.name: A Drift by Robert Aperios (Codrops, 2026)
sources.what: The technique of cached glyph canvases bent by one-pixel slices (0.72 sin + 0.28 cos), a five-ghost outline stack with pow(1 - age/5, 1.35) opacity and a cycling phase; re-derived, no files copied (the repo has no licence).

sources.name: Christina Rossetti, “Who Has Seen the Wind?” (Sing-Song, 1872)
